contentFull: Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts AI is changing farming: Are farmers asking the right questions? By Agriland News Team October 24, 2026 2:00 PM Share this article ![Image 1](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsai-is-changing-farming-are-farmers-asking-the-right-questions) Artificial intelligence (AI) is now a feature on many farms, from smart cow collars to locomotion monitoring to laser weeders and automated slurry scrapers. This may have made life easier for some farmers and producers, but before signing up to a new system, should farmers now be asking questions about privacy, data ownership, and who is responsible for what? According to the president of the scientific-technical committee at the Italian Association of Artificial Intelligence Professionals (AIPIA), when it comes to AI, farmers rarely get a view from "someone with no stake in the sale”. This is why Rafael Patron is urging farmers to ask the right questions before bringing AI onto their farms. AIPIA, an independent non-profit based in Rome, brings together developers, data scientists, researchers and consultants, and keeps a public directory of AI professionals for organisations that need that kind of expertise. Questions Patron believes that farmers should look closely at what they think AI could deliver for them. He uses the example of systems that use camera footage of housed cows to build an individual profile for each one. But Parton said: “It does not see the cow at grass in July. "It does not examine a foot, and it cannot tell you why a cow's mobility has dropped.” In an example like this, Patron said farmers should ask the IT supplier which conditions the system is and is not designed to detect, and what happens to the score when cows are out for the summer. He added: “Ask, too, about false alarms; a system that flags too many cows gets ignored within a month. “One that flags too few gives a false sense of security, which is worse.” ![Image 2](https:images.agriland.ieNbDv1M3uGpFt1jdwcHD8pP0eIsVMsWWz419TroM0VYrs:fit:1024:0bg:FFFFFFplainhttps:cdn.agriland.ieuploads202610woman-works-with-multiple-monitors-and-laptop-2026-09-22-03-02-47-utc-scaled.jpg) According to Patron one issue that may not be exactly transparent is who owns the information gathered by AI systems. He said: “Daily footage and scores for every cow add up, over a year, to a detailed record of how a farm is run: stocking, bedding, feeding routines, how quickly problems are picked up. “If the system is part of a buyer's scheme, find out whether the buyer sees the raw scores, a summary, or only what the farm chooses to share. “Ask where the footage is stored, how long it is kept, whether it is used to train the supplier's algorithm, and what you can take with you if you leave the scheme or change supplier.” While Patron said that none of this is necessarily a reason to avoid a system, he believes it is important to get the answers to these questions in writing. Who is in the loop? In the case of cattle monitoring AI, Patron said: “Before installation, agree with your vet which alerts will trigger a visual check and which will go straight onto the herd health plan, and decide who on the farm looks at the dashboard each day.” He advises that AI connected to existing software can help, but only if the scores end up in front of a human with the time and authority to act on the information. Patron said that farmers who get the most from these systems “will probably be the ones who already know their cows well and use the scores to settle arguments with data rather than to replace their own eyes”. He also recommends that it could be useful to visit a farm that has run a similar system for a full year, "ideally one that looks like yours”. translationZh:
人工智能（AI）如今已成为许多农场的标配功能，从智能牛项圈到步态监测，从激光除草机到自动刮粪板，不一而足。这可能让一些农民和生产者的生活变得更轻松，但在签约使用新系统之前，农民是否应该就隐私、数据所有权以及责任归属等问题提出疑问？

意大利人工智能专业人士协会（AIPIA）科技委员会主席表示，在AI问题上，农民很少能听到“与销售没有利益关系的人”的观点。正因如此，拉斐尔·帕特龙敦促农民在将AI引入农场之前问对问题。AIPIA是一家位于罗马的独立非营利组织，汇集了开发者、数据科学家、研究人员和顾问，并为需要此类专业知识的组织维护一份AI专业人士公开名录。

**该问哪些问题**

帕特龙认为，农民应仔细审视他们以为AI能为自己带来什么。他以利用舍饲奶牛摄像头画面为每头牛建立个体档案的系统为例。但帕特龙表示：“它看不到七月在草地上吃草的牛。它不检查蹄部，也无法告诉你某头牛的步态评分为何下降。”

在此类案例中，帕特龙建议农民询问IT供应商：该系统设计用于检测哪些状况、不适用于哪些状况，以及当奶牛夏季出舍放牧时评分会怎样。他还补充道：“还要问误报情况；一个频繁误报的系统一个月内就会被无视。而一个几乎不报警的系统则会给人虚假的安全感，这更糟糕。”

帕特龙指出，一个可能并不完全透明的问题是AI系统所采集信息的归属权。他说：“每头牛的每日录像和评分，一年下来就累积成一份关于农场如何运营的详细记录：存栏密度、垫料、饲喂流程、问题被发现的速度。如果该系统是买方计划的一部分，要弄清楚买方看到的是原始评分、汇总摘要，还是仅限农场选择分享的内容。要问录像存储在哪里、保存多久、是否用于训练供应商的算法，以及如果你退出该计划或更换供应商，你能带走什么。”

尽管帕特龙表示这些都不一定是回避某个系统的理由，但他认为以书面形式获得这些问题的答案很重要。

**谁在闭环中？**

在牛只监测AI的案例中，帕特龙说：“安装前，与你的兽医商定哪些警报会触发目视检查、哪些直接纳入牛群健康计划，并决定农场里谁每天查看仪表盘。”他建议，AI与现有软件连接会有帮助，但前提是评分最终能呈现在一个有时间和权限据此采取行动的人面前。

帕特龙表示，从这些系统中获益最多的农民，“很可能正是那些已经非常了解自己牛群、并用评分以数据来平息争论、而非取代自己双眼的人”。他还建议，参观一个已运行类似系统满一年的农场可能很有用，“最好是一个与你农场情况相似的农场”。
